examples.worked_solution:
Let $u = 1 - x^3.$ Then

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = -3x^2 \quad \Longrightarrow\quad -\dfrac{1}{3} \textrm d u= x^2 \, \textrm d x,
$$

and we can solve the resulting integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{3}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{3}}}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(2\sqrt{u})+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{u}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1-{x}^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Calculate the integral of $\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+10}$ with respect to $x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{3}+10.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

and we can solve the resulting integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+10}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}+10}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{3}+10|+C\end{aligned}
$$
